newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown says has tightened monetary framework.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown says has tightened monetary framework.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Thursday that his changes to the UK inflation target represented a tightening of the monetary policy framework.
"I have tightened up the framework, I have made it more rigorous and I have made it more open," he told parliament.

The inflation target range under the previous Conservative government had been one to four percent. Under the new arrangements, if inflation went above 3.5 percent, the Governor of the Bank of England would have to write a letter explaining the situation.
"I believe that taken together, the reforms in the Bank of England, the setting up of the monetary policy committee...and this new open procedure will be welcomed both in Britain and abroad."

"It is the best guarantee that we can have the consistently low inflation which has eluded us as a country, as a platform for what everybody wants, which is high and stable levels of growth and employment."
